scope: Same-host DXGI desktop update to NDI decoded BGRX CPU memory. 300 FPS, no display or AI. No source drawing window. Natural desktop content is not controlled.

decisions.region_metadata: Adopt: avoid GPU copy, Map and color conversion for updates proven outside the crop. First frame, cursor mode and unavailable/invalid metadata refresh conservatively.
decisions.readback_copy: Adopt only validated tight-buffer size ranges; padded rows and intermediate sizes retain the row path.
decisions.gpu_uyvy: Reject as default: lower NDI submission call time did not consistently improve decoded-memory latency; additional readback bytes and variable tails.
decisions.bounded_map_polling: Reject: no consistent 416-pixel whole-path improvement; adds busy polling.
decisions.keep_gpu_bindings: Reject: dispatch costs are sub-microsecond at the median with no repeatable whole-path improvement established.
decisions.split_capture_send: Deferred after measurement: observed NDI submission is in tens of microseconds; no sustained submission bottleneck demonstrated. Adding a frame queue at 300 FPS risks 3.33 ms of age.
decisions.pipeline_next_frame_readback: Not adopted: no extra-frame readback pipeline was shipped. Current map wait is around 0.1-0.2 ms and buffering another full frame risks 3.33 ms.

notes: Format/poll timing aggregates use first arrival of each DXGI update; repeated sends excluded from primary latency.
Region-filtered and unfiltered latency populations differ. Do not interpret their latency differences as acceleration.
CPU percentages are whole sender process CPU time divided by wall time, where 100% equals one logical CPU. Natural desktop changes prevent attributing differences to the variants alone.
Readback microbenchmarks measure local processing, not network or AI latency. Trial medians are reported separately.
The final copy benchmark uses two stable buffers for both paths and the previous row-copy algorithm as its reference. An initial one-buffer comparison was replaced and is excluded.
The only-copy oracle performs an unconditional copy from the same acquired desktop texture, then compares every cropped BGRA byte, including frames skipped by the filter.

An initial sandbox loopback attempt and a missing-binary trial aborted and restored the test executable. They are excluded. The first dual-duplication oracle was unsupported by DXGI; the final oracle uses the same acquired texture.
Final release stores the metadata tracker in a once-allocated Box to keep capture state compact; the region decisions and pixel-copy algorithms are unchanged.
